policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'I strive for you, and for them at Laodicea' renders either preposition identically; ὑπὲρ and περὶ with the genitive both give English 'for' here, and no note is mapped to this unit.

ASV 'their hearts may be comforted, they being knit together in love' expresses the participle without marking its case; the nominative (ad sensum) and the genitive (agreeing with the implied persons) both yield 'they being knit together'. The mapped notes are an alternative rendering ('Or, fulness') and a general remark that authorities vary, neither of which names a reading.

ASV 'unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding' fits πᾶν πλοῦτος, πᾶν τὸ πλοῦτος and πάντα πλοῦτον alike: the gender of πλοῦτος is invisible in English, and the article with πᾶς is regularly left untranslated. No mapped textual note distinguishes them.

ASV 'the mystery of God, even Christ' has the single genitive of the base reading; the expansion καὶ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ would require 'of God, and of the Father, and of Christ', which the ASV does not render.

ASV 'all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge' is compatible with καὶ γνώσεως and with καὶ τῆς γνώσεως; the added article does not change the English, which does not repeat 'of' in either case. No note is mapped here.
ASV opens 'This I say' with no connective. The ASV renders a resumptive δέ in such formulas ('Now this I say'), so the asyndeton reflects τοῦτο without δέ.
ASV 'that no one may delude you' renders μηδεὶς and μή τις identically; the negation is carried by the same English words either way, and no note is mapped to this unit.

ASV 'established in your faith' with the note 'Or, by' turns on English wording, not on the presence of ἐν: the bare dative τῇ πίστει is rendered 'in ... faith' as readily as ἐν τῇ πίστει. The chapter's mapped textual note ('insert in it') concerns ἐν αὐτῇ at περισσεύοντες, not this unit.
ASV reads 'abounding in thanksgiving' without 'in it', and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities insert in it' places ἐν αὐτῇ outside the adopted text.
ASV 'in the putting off of the body of the flesh' lacks any rendering of τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν; the RP reading would give 'the body of the sins of the flesh'.
ASV 'buried with him in baptism' renders βαπτισμῷ and βαπτίσματι alike; the two nouns are not distinguished in English and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'raised him from the dead' fits ἐκ νεκρῶν and ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν equally; English supplies 'the' with the substantival adjective regardless of the Greek article.

ASV 'being dead through your trespasses' does not settle the preposition: the ASV renders both the bare dative of cause and ἐν with 'through' in this idiom (cf. its handling of the same phrase elsewhere). No note is mapped to this unit.
ASV 'in meat, or in drink, or in respect of a feast day' has the disjunctive ἢ at this point; the variant καὶ would give 'and in respect of'.
ASV 'but the body is Christ's' does not show whether the genitive Χριστοῦ carried the article; English marks the possessive the same way either way, and no note is mapped here.

ASV 'dwelling in the things which he hath seen' renders ἃ ἑόρακεν without the negative, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many authorities, some ancient, insert not' explicitly places μὴ outside the adopted text.
